requirements_summary: Primary workload: low-latency clinical triage chat + PDF/notes summarization and fast embedding-based search. Targets: P95 < 60ms, P99 < 120ms for single-turn chat at 128-token context; sustained throughput goal 200 reqs/s with 95% < 100ms. Cost sensitive: want 50–70% reduction vs current cloud provider spend. Key asks: automatic prefix/KV caching for templated prompts, smart batching that preserves 95ms latency SLO, and an int8/4-bit quantization path with accuracy regression monitoring. Must support private VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS and audit logs; retention controls for PHI and ability to pin model versions for canary rollouts. Also requested Redwood-perf harness output and guidance to replicate benches internally.
notes:
- Profiled current infra: 3x N+1 GPU autoscaling groups, high variance during peak triage windows; main cost driver = per-token billing + lack of KV caching.
- Customer quote: "We need predictable P99s during morning triage spikes — current spikes double response times and degrade clinician trust."
- Technical preferences: prefer open Llama-family variant (finetuned) but willing to test a Redwood-curated quantized candidate. Concerned about hallucination rates post-quantization; wants evaluation harness.
- POC scope discussed: (1) Dedicated 2x A100-equivalent nodes for 3 weeks, (2) baseline perf with float32 model, (3) int8/int4 quantized runs with eval set (1000 clinical prompts), (4) caching + batching config tuning and metric dashboarding.
- Perf metrics requested: token/sec, latency distribution (P50/P95/P99), cost per 1k tokens, quality regressions per eval set, cache hit ratio.
- Ops asks: route policy by region and failover variant (smaller cheaper model) when capacity constrained. Also auto-fallback if quantized variant exceeds regression threshold.
- Security/Compliance: legal needs vendor SOC2 report; infra team requires private control plane + VPC peering and HSM-backed KMS.
- Internal stakeholders: CTO Somesh Patel (decision-maker), Head of ML Ops Tara Nguyen (technical lead), Procurement: Daniel Romero.
- Short term blocker: procurement wants detailed TCO and quantization accuracy report before commit.
- Long notes: customer is highly risk-averse re: PHI; wants rollback plan and canary strategy that Redwood supports.
- Open items: exact model family to benchmark, acceptance thresholds for quality delta post-quantization, formal statement of work timeline.
other_comments: Preference for a performance-first POC rather than feature-first. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching thresholds, cache TTLs) and a reproducible perf harness. Wants explicit fallback routing: dedicated -> hosted-dedicated -> smaller quantized variant.
